    /\ avail \in 0..Total
    /\ reserved \in 0..Total
    /\ loaned \in 0..Total
    /\ inTransit \in 0..Total
    /\ expiry \in 0..MaxTime

Init ==
    /\ now = 0
    /\ avail = Total
    /\ reserved = 0
    /\ loaned = 0
    /\ inTransit = 0
    /\ expiry = 0

Reserve ==
    /\ avail > 0
    /\ avail' = avail - 1
    /\ reserved' = reserved + 1
    /\ expiry' = IF now + Term > MaxTime THEN MaxTime ELSE now + Term
    /\ UNCHANGED <<now, loaned, inTransit>>

Tick ==
    /\ now < MaxTime
    /\ now' = now + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<avail, reserved, loaned, inTransit, expiry>>

    /\ reserved > 0
    /\ now >= expiry
    /\ reserved' = reserved - 1
    /\ avail' = avail + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<now, loaned, inTransit, expiry>>

Checkout ==
    /\ reserved > 0
    /\ reserved' = reserved - 1
    /\ loaned' = loaned + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<now, avail, inTransit, expiry>>

    /\ UNCHANGED <<now, avail, reserved, expiry>>

CONSTANTS
    Total = 2
    MaxTime = 3
    Term = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT Conservation
nl:
Scenario: a library book reservation system

A title has a fixed number of physical copies; none are ever created or
destroyed, they only move between four places: available on the shelf, reserved
under a lease, loaned out, or in return-transit. The grand total of copies is
constant.

Reservations use lease-based ownership with expiry against a shared clock. A
patron reserves an available copy, moving it into the reserved pool with a lease
that expires at a set time. Time advances by ticks; when a reservation's lease
expires the copy returns to the shelf. A reserved copy may instead be checked
out, moving it into the loaned pool. When a loaned copy is returned it does not
land on the shelf immediately: return notices can be reordered, so the copy
first enters a return-transit pool and is later settled back onto the shelf in
whatever order the notices are processed.

Actions: Reserve (an available copy moves into the reserved pool under a lease),
Tick (the clock advances), ExpireRes (a reserved copy whose lease has expired
returns to the shelf), Checkout (a reserved copy moves into the loaned pool),
Return (a loaned copy moves into return-transit), and Settle (a return-transit
copy is placed back on the shelf).

SAFETY PROPERTY: the copies available, reserved, loaned, and in return-transit
always sum to the fixed total, so no copy is ever created or destroyed.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od2m2p3t0 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Robots, Slots

VARIABLES phase, prop, votes, owner, claim, crashed

vars == <<phase, prop, votes, owner, claim, crashed>>

Idle == "idle"
Voting == "voting"
Free == "free"
NoClaim == "none"
NoProp == "none"
NoVote == "novote"
Yes == "yes"
No == "no"

Props == [slot : Slots, robot : Robots]

TypeOK ==
    /\ phase \in {Idle, Voting}
    /\ prop \in Props \cup {NoProp}
    /\ votes \in [Robots -> {NoVote, Yes, No}]
    /\ owner \in [Slots -> Robots \cup {Free}]
    /\ claim \in [Robots -> Slots \cup {NoClaim}]
    /\ crashed \in SUBSET Robots

Init ==
    /\ phase = Idle
    /\ prop = NoProp
    /\ votes = [r \in Robots |-> NoVote]
    /\ owner = [s \in Slots |-> Free]
    /\ claim = [r \in Robots |-> NoClaim]
    /\ crashed = {}

Propose(s, r) ==
    /\ phase = Idle
    /\ owner[s] = Free
    /\ claim[r] = NoClaim
    /\ r \notin crashed
    /\ phase' = Voting
    /\ prop' = [slot |-> s, robot |-> r]
    /\ votes' = [rb \in Robots |-> NoVote]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, claim, crashed>>

Vote(rb, v) ==
    /\ phase = Voting
    /\ rb \notin crashed
    /\ votes[rb] = NoVote
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![rb] = v]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, prop, owner, claim, crashed>>

Commit ==
    /\ phase = Voting
    /\ \A rb \in Robots \ crashed : votes[rb] = Yes
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![prop.slot] = prop.robot]
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![prop.robot] = prop.slot]
    /\ phase' = Idle
    /\ prop' = NoProp
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, crashed>>

Abort ==
    /\ phase = Voting
    /\ \E rb \in Robots \ crashed : votes[rb] = No
    /\ phase' = Idle
    /\ prop' = NoProp
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, owner, claim, crashed>>

Release(r) ==
    /\ claim[r] # NoClaim
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![claim[r]] = Free]
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![r] = NoClaim]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, prop, votes, crashed>>

Crash(r) ==
    /\ r \notin crashed
    /\ (crashed \cup {r}) # Robots
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, prop, votes, owner, claim>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Slots, r \in Robots : Propose(s, r)
    \/ \E rb \in Robots, v \in {Yes, No} : Vote(rb, v)
    \/ Commit
    \/ Abort
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Release(r)
    \/ \E r \in Robots : Crash(r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoDoubleAllocation ==
    \A r \in Robots : claim[r] # NoClaim => owner[claim[r]] = r

=============================================================================
nl:
Scenario: a warehouse robot fleet

Two robots are assigned charging slots through two-phase commit across the fleet.
A coordinator proposes assigning a specific free slot to a specific claimless
robot and opens a voting round; every live robot must vote. If all live robots
vote yes the round commits, installing the authoritative slot ownership and the
robot's local claim together. If any live robot votes no, the round aborts and
no assignment is made. A robot may later release its slot, clearing both its
claim and the slot's ownership.

The dispatcher keeps an authoritative owner for each slot (a robot, or "free"),
and each robot keeps a local claim naming the one slot it holds, if any. A commit
sets both sides atomically, and a release clears both, so the two views never
disagree.

One participant can crash silently: a robot may crash without warning; a crashed
robot no longer votes, and a round commits on the yes votes of the live robots.
At least one robot always stays live.

Actions: Propose (the coordinator opens a round assigning a free slot to a
claimless robot), Vote (a live robot casts yes or no in the open round), Commit
(a round with all live robots voting yes installs the ownership and claim), Abort
(a round with any no vote is dropped), Release (a robot clears its claim and frees
its slot), and Crash (a robot crashes silently while the last live robot is never
crashed).

SAFETY PROPERTY: every robot that holds a claim is the authoritative owner of the
slot it claims, so no slot is ever double-allocated to two robots at once.

VARIABLES now, holder, expiry, value, snap, high

vars == <<now, holder, expiry, value, snap, high>>

NoOne == "none"

TypeOK ==
    /\ now \in 0..MaxTime
    /\ holder \in Ctrls \cup {NoOne}
    /\ expiry \in 0..MaxTime
    /\ value \in 0..MaxV
    /\ snap \in [Ctrls -> 0..MaxV]
    /\ high \in 0..MaxV

Init ==
    /\ now = 0
    /\ holder = NoOne
    /\ expiry = 0
    /\ value = 0
    /\ snap = [c \in Ctrls |-> 0]
    /\ high = 0

Acquire(c) ==
    /\ holder = NoOne
    /\ holder' = c
    /\ expiry' = IF now + Term > MaxTime THEN MaxTime ELSE now + Term
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = value]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<now, value, high>>

Tick ==
    /\ now < MaxTime
    /\ now' = now + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, expiry, value, snap, high>>

Write(c) ==
    /\ holder = c
    /\ now <= expiry
    /\ snap[c] = value
    /\ value < MaxV
    /\ value' = snap[c] + 1
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![c] = snap[c] + 1]
    /\ high' = IF snap[c] + 1 > high THEN snap[c] + 1 ELSE high
    /\ UNCHANGED <<now, holder, expiry>>

    /\ holder = c
    /\ holder' = NoOne
    /\ UNCHANGED <<now, expiry, value, snap, high>>

Expire ==
    /\ holder # NoOne
    /\ now > expiry
    /\ holder' = NoOne
    /\ UNCHANGED <<now, expiry, value, snap, high>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Ctrls : Acquire(c)
    \/ Tick
    \/ \E c \in Ctrls : Write(c)
    \/ \E c \in Ctrls : Release(c)
    \/ Expire

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoRegression == value >= high

=============================================================================

CONSTANTS
    Ctrls = {g1, g2}
    MaxV = 3
    MaxTime = 3
    Term = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoRegression
nl:
Scenario: a power-grid load shedder

Grid controllers revise one shared setpoint record -- an integer that only ever
climbs as load is progressively shed. Write access uses lease-based ownership
with expiry against a shared clock: a controller takes a lease naming it holder
until an expiry time, and only the current holder, before expiry, may revise the
setpoint.

Revising is a blind read-modify-write. On acquiring its lease the holder
snapshots the live setpoint; each revision writes back its snapshot-plus-one and
advances its snapshot in lockstep, and a revision is refused unless the snapshot
still equals the live setpoint. The system also tracks the highest setpoint ever
committed. Because the lease is exclusive, a healthy holder's snapshot stays
equal to the live value, so its blind write always moves the setpoint up to a
fresh high -- never backward over another controller's revision.

A participant can be slow but not failed: a controller may take a lease,
snapshot, and then lag while the clock advances past its expiry. Its lease then
lapses and the record reverts to unowned, so the slow controller cannot write on
a stale snapshot; a new holder re-snapshots the current value first. No
controller is lost.

Actions: Acquire (an idle-lease controller takes a lease until now-plus-term and
snapshots the setpoint), Tick (the clock advances), Write (the holder, before
expiry and with a snapshot still equal to the live setpoint, commits its
snapshot-plus-one and lifts the recorded high), Release (the holder gives up its
lease), and Expire (a lapsed lease is cleared).

SAFETY PROPERTY: the live setpoint is always at least the highest value ever
committed, so no blind revision ever regressed the record over another
controller's update -- no update was lost.

    /\ inUse[i] < SharedCap
    /\ queued' = [queued EXCEPT ![i] = queued[i] - 1]

    /\ UNCHANGED <<finished, rejected>>

    /\ UNCHANGED <<queued, rejected>>

CONSTANTS
    SharedCap = 2
    QCap = 2
    MaxFin = 2
    MaxRej = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT WithinSharedCapacity
nl:
Scenario: a warehouse robot fleet

Two independent picking instances share one common docking pool of fixed
capacity. Each instance runs its own bounded work queue with backpressure:
pending pick jobs wait in a queue that holds at most a fixed number, and when an
instance's queue is full the queue rejects further arrivals rather than growing.

Starting a job moves it from an instance's queue into an active docking slot, but
only while the shared pool still has room -- the two instances together may never
hold more active slots than the shared capacity. Finishing a job frees its
docking slot back to the shared pool. Because both instances draw active slots
from the same pool, a burst in one instance can starve the other, but neither can
push the shared occupancy past its limit.

Actions: Enqueue (an instance admits a job into its queue while below capacity),
Reject (an instance whose queue is full turns away an arrival, recording the
backpressure), Start (an instance moves a queued job into an active docking slot
while the shared pool has room), and Finish (an instance completes an active job,
freeing its docking slot).

SAFETY PROPERTY: the active docking slots held by the two instances together
never exceed the shared pool capacity.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od11m0p1t5 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Workers, MaxVer, MaxOverride

VARIABLES version, base, snapVer, phase, budget

vars == <<version, base, snapVer, phase, budget>>

Idle == "idle"
Armed == "armed"

TypeOK ==
    /\ version \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ base \in 0..MaxVer
    /\ snapVer \in [Workers -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ phase \in [Workers -> {Idle, Armed}]
    /\ budget \in 0..MaxOverride

Init ==
    /\ version = 0
    /\ base = 0
    /\ snapVer = [w \in Workers |-> 0]
    /\ phase = [w \in Workers |-> Idle]
    /\ budget = MaxOverride

Arm(w) ==
    /\ phase[w] = Idle
    /\ snapVer' = [snapVer EXCEPT ![w] = version]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![w] = Armed]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, base, budget>>

Committable(w) ==
    /\ phase[w] = Armed
    /\ snapVer[w] = version
    /\ version < MaxVer

Commit(w) ==
    /\ Committable(w)
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ base' = snapVer[w]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![w] = Idle]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snapVer, budget>>

Retry(w) ==
    /\ phase[w] = Armed
    /\ ~Committable(w)
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![w] = Idle]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, base, snapVer, budget>>

AdminForce ==
    /\ budget > 0
    /\ version < MaxVer
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ base' = version
    /\ budget' = budget - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snapVer, phase>>

Next ==
    \/ \E w \in Workers : Arm(w)
    \/ \E w \in Workers : Commit(w)
    \/ \E w \in Workers : Retry(w)
    \/ AdminForce

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoLostUpdate == version = 0 \/ base = version - 1

CONSTANTS
    Workers = {w1, w2}
    MaxVer = 3
    MaxOverride = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
Scenario: a print shop job spooler

Two workers revise one shared spool record that carries a version counter and the
base version its latest revision was built upon. They coordinate with optimistic
locking and retry. A worker arms a revision by snapshotting the live version; it
commits as a compare-and-swap, succeeding only if the live version still equals
its snapshot. A successful commit advances the version by one and stamps the
snapshot as the new base. If the snapshot is stale -- or the record is already at
its maximum -- the worker cannot commit and retries by disarming. This read-check
is what stops one worker's revision from silently overwriting another's.

There is a privileged admin override: an administrator may force the version to
advance even without an armed, matching snapshot, but the override still stamps
the just-superseded version as the base, so a forced revision keeps the record's
lineage intact. The override budget is finite.

Actions: Arm (an idle worker snapshots the live version), Commit (an armed worker
whose snapshot still equals the live version advances the version and stamps its
snapshot as base), Retry (an armed worker that cannot commit disarms), and
AdminForce (the admin advances the version, stamping the superseded version as
base).

SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever the record has been revised at least once, its base is
exactly one less than its live version, so every revision built on the
immediately preceding one and no update was lost.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od13m1p6t1 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Machines, MaxGen

VARIABLES gen, readGen, granted, acting

vars == <<gen, readGen, granted, acting>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ gen \in 0..MaxGen
    /\ readGen \in [Machines -> 0..MaxGen]
    /\ granted \in [Machines -> 0..MaxGen]
    /\ acting \in [Machines -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
    /\ gen = 0
    /\ readGen = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
    /\ granted = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
    /\ acting = [m \in Machines |-> FALSE]

Read(m) ==
    /\ readGen' = [readGen EXCEPT ![m] = gen]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<gen, granted, acting>>

Grant(m) ==
    /\ granted' = [granted EXCEPT ![m] = readGen[m]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<gen, readGen, acting>>

Act(m) ==
    /\ granted[m] = gen
    /\ ~acting[m]
    /\ acting' = [acting EXCEPT ![m] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<gen, readGen, granted>>

Pass ==
    /\ gen < MaxGen
    /\ gen' = gen + 1
    /\ acting' = [m \in Machines |-> FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<readGen, granted>>

Stop(m) ==
    /\ acting[m]
    /\ acting' = [acting EXCEPT ![m] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<gen, readGen, granted>>

Next ==
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Read(m)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Grant(m)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Act(m)
    \/ Pass
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Stop(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoStaleAction ==
    \A m \in Machines : acting[m] => granted[m] = gen

CONSTANTS
    Machines = {y1, y2}
    MaxGen = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoStaleAction
nl:
Scenario: a vending machine network

Two machines in a network take turns driving the shared restock bus, coordinated
by a token ring whose current holder is identified by a token generation counter.
A machine may drive the bus only while its recorded grant generation equals the
live token generation.

Because grant messages can be reordered, a machine does not stamp the live
generation directly. It first reads the token generation into a private snapshot,
and later stamps that snapshot as its grant -- but by the time it stamps, the
snapshot may already be stale if the token was passed on in between. Driving is
allowed only when the stamped grant generation still equals the live generation,
so a machine that stamped an out-of-date snapshot cannot drive.

Passing the token advances the generation and, as a hard barrier, halts every
machine currently driving, so no machine keeps driving on a superseded grant.

Actions: Read (a machine snapshots the live token generation), Grant (a machine
stamps its snapshot as its grant generation, which may already be stale), Act (a
machine whose grant generation still equals the live generation begins driving
the bus), Pass (the token generation advances and all driving halts), and Stop (a
driving machine stops).

SAFETY PROPERTY: a machine drives the bus only if its recorded grant generation
equals the live token generation, so no stale or unauthorized machine ever drives
on an out-of-date grant.

    /\ reqs' = reqs \cup {[student |-> st, seat |-> s]}

    /\ claim[r.student] = NoClaim
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![r.seat] = r.student]
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![r.student] = r.seat]
    /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![r.student] = IF now + Term > MaxTime THEN MaxTime ELSE now + Term]
    /\ reqs' = reqs \ {r}

    /\ now' = now + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, claim, expiry, reqs>>

    /\ now >= expiry[st]
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![claim[st]] = Free]
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![st] = NoClaim]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<now, expiry, reqs>>

    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![claim[st]] = Free]
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![st] = NoClaim]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<now, expiry, reqs>>

    /\ (owner[r.seat] # Free \/ claim[r.student] # NoClaim)

    \/ Tick
    \/ \E st \in Students : Expire(st)
    \/ \E st \in Students : Release(st)
    \/ \E r \in Requests : DropReq(r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

    \A st \in Students : claim[st] # NoClaim => owner[claim[st]] = st

CONSTANTS
    Students = {u1, u2}
    Seats = {c1, c2}
    MaxTime = 2
    Term = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
nl:
Scenario: a university course-registration system

Students hold seats in courses under lease-based ownership with expiry against a
shared clock. The registrar keeps an authoritative owner for each seat (a
student, or "free"), and each student keeps a local claim naming the one seat it
holds, if any. A grant sets both together and stamps a lease expiry; when a lease
lapses, or a student releases, both the ownership and the claim are cleared
together, so the two views never disagree.

Enrollment requests can be reordered: students drop requests into a shared pool
that the registrar processes in any order. A pooled request is granted only if
its seat is still free and the student still holds no claim; otherwise it simply
waits or is discarded.

Actions: Request (a student drops a seat request into the shared pool), Grant
(the registrar processes a pooled request whose seat is free and whose student is
claimless, installing the ownership and claim and stamping a lease), Tick (the
clock advances), Expire (a student whose lease has lapsed has its seat and claim
cleared together), Release (a student clears its claim and frees its seat), and
DropReq (an unsatisfiable pooled request is discarded).

SAFETY PROPERTY: every student that holds a claim is the authoritative owner of
the seat it claims, so no seat is ever double-allocated to two students at once.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od11m8p5t3 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

VARIABLES coarse, fine, sealCount, sealedBy

vars == <<coarse, fine, sealCount, sealedBy>>

Free == "free"
NoOne == "none"

TypeOK ==
    /\ coarse \in Ctrls \cup {Free}
    /\ fine \in Ctrls \cup {Free}
    /\ sealCount \in 0..MaxSeal
    /\ sealedBy \in Ctrls \cup {NoOne}

Init ==
    /\ coarse = Free
    /\ fine = Free
    /\ sealCount = 0
    /\ sealedBy = NoOne

AcquireCoarse(c) ==
    /\ coarse = Free
    /\ coarse' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, sealCount, sealedBy>>

AcquireFine(c) ==
    /\ coarse = c
    /\ fine = Free
    /\ fine' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, sealCount, sealedBy>>

Seal(c) ==
    /\ coarse = c
    /\ fine = c
    /\ sealCount = 0
    /\ sealCount' = sealCount + 1
    /\ sealedBy' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine>>

ReleaseFine(c) ==
    /\ fine = c

nl:
Scenario: a print shop job spooler

Finalizing a print batch is irreversible: once the batch is sealed to the press
it can never be unsealed, and it must be sealed at most once. Sealing is guarded
by hierarchical locks, coarse then fine. A controller must first take the coarse
batch lock and only then the fine seal lock; it may seal only while it holds
both. After the seal it may release the fine and then the coarse lock.

A participant can be slow but not failed: a controller may take both locks and
then lag arbitrarily before sealing. Because the locks are exclusive and taken in
coarse-before-fine order, no other controller can be positioned to seal
concurrently, and the seal step itself fires only while the batch has not yet
been sealed. A slow controller therefore delays the seal but can never cause a
second one.

coarse holder takes the free fine lock), Seal (a controller holding both locks
seals the batch, if it has not been sealed yet, recording itself as sealer),

controller holding no fine lock releases the coarse lock).

nl:
Scenario: an airport baggage router

Router nodes revise one shared routing-table record -- a value with a version
counter -- and each revision is agreed by two-phase commit across the nodes. A
coordinator proposes a revision by snapshotting the record's current value and
version, then opens a voting round in which every node must vote. The revision is
a blind read-modify-write: on commit the coordinator writes back its snapshot
value plus one, not a re-read of the live value.

A commit fires only if all nodes vote yes and the snapshot version still equals
the live version, proving no other revision landed since the snapshot. It then
advances both the value and the version by one. If any node votes no, or the
record is already at its maximum, the round aborts and nothing changes.

A participant can be slow but not failed: a node may delay its vote arbitrarily.
The round simply waits for it; because no revision can commit mid-round, the
coordinator's snapshot stays current, and the eventual blind write never
overwrites an intervening revision. No node is lost, it merely lags.

round), Vote (a node casts yes or no -- votes may arrive slowly and in any
order), Commit (a unanimous round whose snapshot version is still live writes the
snapshot-plus-one and advances the version), and Abort (a round with a no vote,
or against a maxed record, is dropped).

SAFETY PROPERTY: the shared value always equals the version counter, so no blind
revision ever overwrote another's contribution -- no update is lost.

nl:
Scenario: a stock exchange opening auction

Two order-book instances -- the buy book and the sell book -- feed one shared
matching engine that can hold at most a fixed number of live orders at once. The
count of live orders sits in one shared register, and both instances coordinate
on it with optimistic locking and retry.

Placing an order is a blind read-modify-write. An instance first reads the live
order count into a private snapshot, then places by writing back its
snapshot-plus-one -- but the write commits only as a compare-and-swap: the live
count must still equal the snapshot, and it must be below the shared capacity. If
another instance placed or filled in between, the snapshot is stale and the
compare-and-swap does not fire, so the instance reads again to retry. Filling an
order likewise reads and then writes the snapshot-minus-one under a
compare-and-swap.

one book competes with the other, yet neither can push the engine past its
capacity.

whose snapshot still matches the live count, while below capacity, increments the
count and records a placement), Fill (an instance whose snapshot still matches the
non-empty live count decrements it and records a fill), and Cancel (an instance
whose snapshot still matches the non-empty live count decrements it and records a
cancellation).

SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of live orders in the shared matching engine never
exceeds the shared capacity.

nl:
Scenario: a multiplayer game lobby matchmaker

Three matchmaking workers contend for the single ranked-match slot, the critical
resource. Access uses lease-based ownership with expiry against a shared clock: a
worker acquires a lease naming it holder until an expiry time, and only the
current holder, while its lease is in force, may occupy the slot. Entering the
slot is a separate step from holding the lease, and on exit the worker leaves the
slot and drops its lease. Time advances by ticks; when a lease reaches its expiry
it lapses, and expiry both clears the holder and evicts any occupant, so an
expired lease never strands an occupant.

clearing the holder and its occupancy together, or force-grant the free slot's
lease to a worker directly. The override budget is finite, and every override
keeps the holder-and-occupant coupling intact so it can never leave two workers
in the slot.

holder occupies the slot while its lease is in force), Exit (the occupant leaves
and drops the lease), Tick (the clock advances), Expire (a lapsed lease is
cleared and its occupant evicted), AdminEvict (the admin clears the holder and
its occupant together), and AdminGrant (the admin grants the free lease to a
worker directly).

SAFETY PROPERTY: a worker occupies the ranked-match slot only if it is the
current lease holder, so at most one worker is ever in the slot at a time.

nl:
Scenario: a print shop job spooler

Two workers revise one shared spool record -- a value paired with a version
counter -- through a bounded work queue with backpressure. Prepared revision
requests wait in a queue holding at most a fixed number of entries; when the
queue is full, no new request may be prepared.

A prepared request records the version it read. Applying it is a blind
read-modify-write committed under a compare-and-swap: the request commits only if
the version it read still equals the live version, in which case the value is
written to that read version plus one and the version advances by one. Because a
healthy record keeps its value equal to its version, this write always lands the
value exactly one ahead in step with the version. A request whose read version is
stale, or that cannot commit because the record is maxed, is discarded and
re-prepared. This read-check stops one worker's revision from overwriting
another's.

There is a privileged admin override: an administrator may force a queued request
to commit even without a matching read version, advancing the value and version
together so the record stays consistent. The override budget is finite.

the queue is below capacity), Apply (a queued request whose read version still
matches the live version writes the read-plus-one value and advances the
version), Discard (a queued request that cannot commit is dropped), and
AdminApply (the admin forces a queued request to commit, advancing the value and
version together).

SAFETY PROPERTY: the shared value always equals the version counter, so no blind
revision ever overwrote another worker's contribution -- no update is lost.

nl:
Scenario: a print shop job spooler

A fixed number of print credits circulate through the shop; none are ever created
or destroyed, they only move between three pools: the free pool, the active pool
(credits attached to running jobs), and the transit pool (credits being reconciled
back). A single dispatcher, chosen by leader election with failover, is the sole
mover of credits; each election takes a strictly higher epoch so a superseded
dispatcher is replaced.

The dispatcher moves one credit at a time: dispatching pulls a credit from the
free pool into the active pool, completing moves an active credit into transit,
and settling returns a transit credit to the free pool. Every move relocates
exactly one credit and leaves the grand total untouched.

Capacity changes at runtime: an active-pool cap toggles between a low and a high
value, and the dispatcher may dispatch only while the active pool is below the
current cap. The cap is never set below the credits already active.

(the dispatcher moves one credit from the free pool to the active pool while below
the cap), Complete (the dispatcher moves one active credit into transit), Settle
(the dispatcher returns one transit credit to the free pool), and ChangeCap (the
active-pool cap is set to a value no smaller than the active count).

total, so no credit is ever created or destroyed.

nl:
Scenario: a print shop job spooler

Two workers claim exclusive output trays through optimistic locking with retry.
The spooler keeps an authoritative owner for each tray (a worker, or "free"), and
each worker keeps a local claim naming the one tray it holds, if any.

A worker takes a tray in two steps. It first observes a free-looking tray and
records it as its target. It then commits the claim as a compare-and-swap: the
grab succeeds only if the target tray is still free and the worker still holds no
claim, in which case it installs the tray's ownership and the worker's claim
together. If another worker grabbed the tray in between, the target is no longer
free, the compare-and-swap does not fire, and the worker retries by dropping its
target. Releasing clears both the worker's claim and the tray's ownership.

One participant can crash silently: a worker may crash at any point, keeping
whatever claim it holds; a crashed worker takes no further steps. At least one
worker always stays live.

Actions: Observe (an idle live worker records a free-looking tray as its target),
Claim (a targeting worker whose target tray is still free installs the ownership
and its claim together), Retry (a targeting worker whose target is no longer free
drops its target), Release (a worker clears its claim and frees its tray), and
Crash (a worker crashes silently while the last live worker is never crashed).

SAFETY PROPERTY: every worker that holds a claim is the authoritative owner of the
tray it claims, so no tray is ever double-allocated to two workers at once.

Scenario: a warehouse robot fleet

Two robots are assigned charging slots by a dispatcher chosen through leader
election with failover; each election takes a strictly higher epoch so a
superseded dispatcher is replaced. The dispatcher keeps an authoritative
assignment for each slot (a robot, or "free").

Assignment and starting are decoupled because a participant can be slow but not
failed. When the dispatcher assigns a free slot to an idle robot, the robot does
not begin at once: it holds the assignment as pending and may lag arbitrarily
before starting work on it. Because the dispatcher will not reassign a slot that
is still assigned, a slow robot's pending slot is held for it, and only when it
finally starts does it become the working slot. Finishing frees the slot's
assignment and clears the robot's work.

(the dispatcher assigns a free slot to an idle robot, which holds it pending),

Scenario: a blood-bank inventory tracker

Discarding a flagged blood unit is irreversible: once discarded it is gone for

node must vote. The discard commits only if all live nodes vote yes and the unit
has not already been discarded, firing the irreversible discard exactly once. If

has already happened, but the discard itself never repeats.

Scenario: a warehouse robot fleet

Robots may enter a shared hazardous staging zone that holds at most a fixed
number of robots at once. Entry is gated by quorum voting on each action: a robot
that wants to enter first raises a proposal, and the fleet votes on it. The robot
is admitted only once a quorum of yes votes has been gathered and only while the
zone is below its capacity; admission adds it to the zone. If the zone is full or
the proposal cannot reach quorum, the proposal is rejected. A robot in the zone
may leave at any time, freeing space.

in any order, so a proposal simply waits for enough of the fleet to weigh in. No
voter is lost; the proposal makes progress as votes trickle in.

ballots), Vote (a robot casts yes or no on the open proposal -- votes may arrive
slowly), Admit (a proposal with a yes quorum enters the zone while it is below
capacity), Reject (a proposal that cannot proceed -- zone full or a no vote
present -- is dropped), and Leave (a robot in the zone leaves).

SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of robots in the staging zone never exceeds the zone
capacity.

nl:
Scenario: a hospital operating-room scheduler

Scheduler nodes maintain one shared set of confirmed room bookings, and each
addition is agreed by two-phase commit across the nodes. A coordinator proposes
adding a booking, snapshotting the current booking set, and opens a voting round;
every node must vote. The commit is a blind rewrite: it writes back its snapshot
with the new booking folded in, rather than re-reading the live set.

The commit fires only if all nodes vote yes and the coordinator's snapshot still
equals the live booking set, proving no other addition landed since the snapshot.
That freshness check is what stops a blind rewrite from dropping a booking another
round added. If any node votes no, the round aborts and the set is unchanged.

A participant can be slow but not failed: a node may delay its vote arbitrarily,
and the round simply waits. Because no commit can land mid-round, the
coordinator's snapshot stays current and its rewrite never discards an
intervening booking. No node is lost.

booking), Vote (a node casts yes or no -- votes may arrive slowly), Commit (a
unanimous round whose snapshot still equals the live set folds the booking in),
and Abort (a round with a no vote is dropped).

SAFETY PROPERTY: every booking that was ever committed is still present in the
shared booking set, so no blind rewrite ever dropped a booking -- no update is
lost.

Scenario: a wildfire drone surveillance swarm

Two drone squads -- two independent instances -- share one common map of
confirmed sightings, the shared pool both squads fold their observations into.
Writes to the map are serialized by a single coordinator chosen through leader
election with failover; each election takes a strictly higher epoch so a
superseded coordinator is replaced.

Folding is a read-modify-write. When a coordinator is elected it snapshots the
current map into a private buffer; each merge writes back its buffer with a new
observation added, and refreshes its buffer to match. Because only the current
coordinator writes, its snapshot stays equal to the live map, so its blind write
never overwrites an observation another merge added. This is what keeps the shared
pool from losing a squad's contribution.

snapshots the map), Merge (the coordinator writes its buffer plus a new
observation from either squad into the map, records the contribution, and
refreshes its buffer), Refresh (the coordinator re-snapshots the live map), and
StepDown (the coordinator relinquishes its role).

SAFETY PROPERTY: every observation that was ever contributed to the shared map is
still present in it, so no squad's sighting is ever lost by a blind overwrite.

Scenario: a blood-bank inventory tracker

Blood units are placed into storage fridges through a bounded work queue with
backpressure: pending units wait in a queue that holds at most a fixed number,
and when the queue is full no further unit may be enqueued. The tracker keeps, for
each fridge, its current occupant unit (or "empty"), and for each unit, the fridge
it is placed in (or "none").

A placement ties both sides together: placing a queued unit into an empty fridge
records the fridge's occupant and the unit's location at once, removing it from
the queue. Removing a unit clears both and marks the unit completed; completed
units may later be reopened for re-storage.

There is a privileged admin override. An administrator may move a placed unit to a
different empty fridge -- clearing its old fridge and setting the new one together
-- or evict a placed unit, clearing its fridge and location together. The override
budget is finite.

Actions: Enqueue (a free, not-completed unit joins the queue while below
capacity), Place (a queued unit is placed into an empty fridge, setting occupant
and location), Remove (a placed unit is cleared and marked completed), Reopen (a
completed unit is returned for re-storage), AdminMove (the admin moves a placed
unit to a different empty fridge, clearing the old fridge), and AdminEvict (the
admin clears a placed unit's fridge and location together).

SAFETY PROPERTY: every unit that records a fridge is in fact the occupant of that
fridge, so no fridge is ever double-allocated to two units at once.

Scenario: a vending machine network

Two machines share a bank of dispense lanes under a strict hierarchical locking
discipline: coarse then fine. There is one coarse bank lock and a separate fine
lock per lane. A machine must first hold the coarse bank lock, then a lane's fine
lock, and it may dispense a lane only while it holds that lane's fine lock. The
tracker records, for each lane, its fine-lock holder, and for each machine, the
lane it is dispensing, if any.

One participant can crash silently: a machine may crash while holding locks and
dispensing, and can then neither stop nor release. An operator reclaim clears a
crashed machine's coarse lock, all its fine locks, and its dispensing state
together in one step, so a lane it held is never handed to another machine while
the crashed one is still recorded as dispensing it. At least one machine always
stays live.

coarse holder takes a free lane's fine lock), Dispense (a machine holding a lane's
fine lock begins dispensing it), Stop (a machine stops dispensing), ReleaseFine (a
machine not dispensing a lane releases its fine lock), ReleaseCoarse (a machine
holding no fine locks and not dispensing releases the coarse lock), Crash (a
machine crashes silently while the last live machine is never crashed), and
Reclaim (a crashed machine's locks and dispensing state are all cleared together).

SAFETY PROPERTY: a machine dispenses a lane only if it holds that lane's fine
lock, so no lane is ever double-allocated to two machines at once.

nl:
Scenario: a university course-registration system

Students contend for the single registration terminal, the critical resource,
under lease-based ownership with expiry against a shared clock. A student that
wants the terminal joins the waiting line. When the terminal is free the registrar
grants a lease to a waiting student, naming it holder until an expiry time and
removing it from the line. Only the current holder, while its lease is in force,
may use the terminal; using is a step separate from holding, and finishing frees
the terminal and drops the lease. The clock advances by ticks, and when a lease
reaches its expiry it lapses -- clearing the holder and ejecting any user, so an
expired lease never leaves a user on the terminal.

There is a privileged admin override. An administrator may grant the free terminal
directly to a student, jumping the line, or revoke a holder, clearing the holder
and its use together. The override budget is finite, and every override keeps the
holder-and-user coupling intact.

Actions: Request (a student joins the waiting line), Grant (the registrar leases
the free terminal to a waiting student), Use (the holder uses the terminal while
its lease is in force), Done (the user finishes and drops the lease), Tick (the
clock advances), Expire (a lapsed lease is cleared and its user ejected),
AdminGrant (the admin leases the free terminal to a student directly), and

nl:
Scenario: a power-grid load shedder

An elected coordinator broadcasts setpoint writes to a shared control record.
Coordination is leader election with failover: at most one coordinator holds the
role, and each election takes a strictly higher epoch so a superseded coordinator
is replaced. The record is the set of writes that have been applied.

Because messages can be reordered, the coordinator's writes do not apply
instantly. Each emitted write first enters an in-flight pool and is later applied
into the record, in whatever order the messages arrive. The system tracks every
write ever emitted. The key discipline is that applying a write moves it from the
in-flight pool into the record -- it never drops a write on the floor -- so an
emitted write is always either already applied or still in flight, never lost.

Actions: Elect (a node becomes coordinator at a strictly higher epoch), Emit (the
coordinator emits a fresh write, placing it in the in-flight pool and recording it
as emitted), Apply (an in-flight write is folded into the record and removed from
the pool, in any order), and StepDown (the coordinator relinquishes its role).

SAFETY PROPERTY: every write ever emitted is either already in the record or still
in the in-flight pool, so no reordered write is ever lost.

    /\ holder = NoOne
    /\ holder' = h
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch, actuating>>

    /\ ~actuating[h]
    /\ actuating' = [actuating EXCEPT ![h] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch, holder>>

nl:
Scenario: a smart-home door lock network

Two independent lock hubs -- instance A with hubs a1 and a2, instance B with hubs
b1 and b2 -- share one master deadbolt, the critical resource that only one hub
may actuate at a time. A dispatcher chosen by leader election with failover grants
a single lock token drawn from the one shared pool; each election takes a strictly
higher epoch so a superseded dispatcher is replaced.

The dispatcher grants the token to a hub only when the token is free. Holding the
token is not the same as actuating: the token holder actuates the deadbolt as a
separate step, and on release it both stops actuating and returns the token to the
shared pool. Because both instances draw the one token from the same pool, a hub
in one instance competes with hubs in the other, yet only the token holder ever
drives the bolt.

Actions: Elect (a hub becomes dispatcher at a strictly higher epoch), Grant (the
dispatcher grants the free shared token to a hub), Actuate (the token holder
actuates the deadbolt), and Release (the actuating hub stops and returns the token
to the shared pool).

SAFETY PROPERTY: a hub actuates the deadbolt only if it currently holds the shared
lock token, so at most one hub ever drives the deadbolt at a time.

VARIABLES epoch, designated, using, cap

vars == <<epoch, designated, using, cap>>

    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ designated \in Presses
    /\ using \in [Presses -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ cap \in {0, 1}

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ designated = CHOOSE p \in Presses : TRUE
    /\ using = [p \in Presses |-> FALSE]
    /\ cap = 1

Reconfigure(p) ==
    /\ (p # designated \/ epoch < MaxEpoch)
    /\ epoch' = IF epoch < MaxEpoch THEN epoch + 1 ELSE epoch
    /\ designated' = p
    /\ using' = [q \in Presses |-> FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED cap

Enter(p) ==
    /\ designated = p
    /\ cap >= 1
    /\ ~using[p]
    /\ using' = [using EXCEPT ![p] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, designated, cap>>

Exit(p) ==
    /\ using[p]
    /\ using' = [using EXCEPT ![p] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, designated, cap>>

ChangeCap ==
    /\ cap' = 1 - cap
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, designated, using>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Presses : Reconfigure(p)
    \/ \E p \in Presses : Enter(p)
    \/ \E p \in Presses : Exit(p)
    \/ ChangeCap

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

MutualExclusion ==
    \A p \in Presses : using[p] => designated = p

nl:
Scenario: a print shop job spooler

Several presses share one binding station, the critical resource that only one
press may use at a time. Access is governed by epoch-numbered reconfiguration: a
configuration epoch designates exactly one press as the current primary, and only
the designated press may use the station. Reconfiguration advances the epoch and
names a new designated press, and as a hard barrier it evicts whoever is currently
using the station, so a reconfiguration never leaves a superseded press at the
binding station.

Capacity changes at runtime: an admission capacity toggles between zero and one,
and while it is zero no press may begin using the station, though the current
designation is undisturbed.

Actions: Reconfigure (the epoch advances, a new press is designated, and any
current user is evicted), Enter (the designated press begins using the station
when capacity is at least one), Exit (the current user stops), and ChangeCap (the
admission capacity is set to zero or one).

SAFETY PROPERTY: a press uses the binding station only if it is the currently
designated press, so at most one press ever uses the station at a time.
